# Riverbend Family Health outreach: Mary Major

## 1. Email sequence

### Email 1: Tuesday, 16 September 2025

**Subject:** Your float-pool question from the 3 Sept webinar

Hi Mary,

Thanks for your question about float-pool nurses at our webinar on 3 September. You said your team burns hours every week filling call-outs by text, and that overtime is your fastest-growing cost. I hear that often, and it's the problem I started ShiftBay to fix.

Here's how it works. When someone calls out, the open shift goes by app to staff who are qualified and available, within your credential and overtime rules. The first person to accept gets the shift, so there are no more text chains. Your float pool can be shared across all 14 sites the same way.

At Northfield Clinics, a 9-site group, call-outs now fill in a median of 22 minutes.

Would a 20-minute call help you judge whether this fits how Riverbend handles call-outs? Reply with a time that suits you and I'll make it work.

Best,
[Name]
Founder, ShiftBay

---

### Email 2: Tuesday, 23 September 2025

**Subject:** Honest overtime numbers

Hi Mary,

Since overtime is the cost you flagged, here are our real numbers.

Across all six ShiftBay customers, overtime hours fell 18% on average after six months. The range is wide. Our lowest result was 8%, and our best was 40% at Northfield Clinics. Pinegate Health (5 clinics) saw 12%.

Where Riverbend would land depends mostly on how much of your overtime comes from last-minute call-outs. We could estimate that together from your own data.

You've opened three new clinics this year and have RN roles open. Covering gaps from your existing staff probably matters more than ever right now.

If it would help, I can introduce you to the operations leads at Northfield or Pinegate so you can hear it from them directly. Would you like me to set that up?

Best,
[Name]

---

### Email 3: Thursday, 2 October 2025

**Subject:** Switching scheduling tools without disruption

Hi Mary,

This is my last note for now.

Scheduling systems are hard to switch mid-contract, so I'd rather be useful early than push you for a fast decision. Implementation takes about six weeks. We import directly from your current system's export format, so your staff records and rules don't need rebuilding.

If your current contract has a notice window, we can plan backwards from it. That way there's no coverage gap and no paying for two systems.

If this is worth exploring, the best next step is a 20-minute call. I'll walk through how a call-out would be filled across your sites, and you can tell me where it wouldn't fit. You can book a time here: [calendar link].

If now isn't the right time, no reply is needed. I'll check back in the new year.

Best,
[Name]

---

## 2. LinkedIn connection note

**Send:** Wednesday, 17 September 2025 (about 245 characters)

> Hi Mary, thanks for your float-pool question at our 3 Sept webinar on last-minute shift gaps. I'm the founder of ShiftBay and would like to stay in touch. Happy to share what's worked for other multi-site clinic groups on call-outs and overtime.

---

## 3. Note to John

John,

Thanks for the push on Riverbend. Here's what I took from your advice and what I left out.

**What I used**

- **Asking for a meeting.** Emails 1 and 3 both ask for a call. I made it a 20-minute call rather than a demo next week. This is our first contact with her, and a smaller ask is easier to accept. The call can turn into a demo.
- **The Northfield result.** It appears in both emails. Email 1 uses the 22-minute median fill time, which speaks directly to her text-message problem. Email 2 gives the 40% figure in context.

**What I rejected**

- **Leading with the 40% cut.** Northfield is our best result, not a typical one.
  - Our average is 18%, and our 12-clinic customer, the closest in size to Riverbend, saw 15%.
  - Mary is a VP of Operations and will ask what the average is. If we anchor her on 40% and she gets 15%, we lose her trust, her renewal and a future reference.
  - Being upfront about the range also makes the Northfield number more believable.
- **Offering 30% off.**
  - My discretion stops at 15%, and only for a multi-year contract.
  - Anything higher needs CFO approval, which has never been granted. Offering it would be a promise we can't keep.
  - I'll hold the 15% in reserve for the actual negotiation. I won't open with a discount.
- **The "sign by Friday" deadline.**
  - Her current contract renews on 30 November 2026 and needs 90 days' notice, so her real decision date is about 1 September 2026.
  - If she signed this Friday, she would pay for two systems for a year. A fake deadline wouldn't move a healthcare VP who has to go through procurement, and it would make us look desperate.
  - The real urgency is giving notice and allowing six weeks for implementation. I raise that gently in Email 3.

**Two other choices**

- **I didn't mention her contract dates.** She hasn't told us them, and quoting them in a first-touch email would feel intrusive.
- **I only named Northfield and Pinegate.** They are the only customers who have agreed to be named and to take reference calls. The other four appear only in the aggregate figures.

**Proposed plan**

1. Get the call booked.
2. Build an overtime estimate from Riverbend's own data.
3. Line up a reference call with Northfield or Pinegate.
4. Aim for a decision in spring 2026, well ahead of her 1 September notice date.

[Name]
